courses.title: Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science, MCA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Propositional and predicate logic
topics.summary: Logical equivalence, inference rules and proof techniques.
notes: Rules of inference: modus ponens, modus tollens, hypothetical syllogism, disjunctive syllogism, resolution.
Normal forms: CNF (conjunction of clauses) and DNF (disjunction of conjunctions).
Proof methods: direct, contrapositive, contradiction, and mathematical induction (base case and inductive step).
outcomes: Derive conclusions with rules of inference

lesson.hook: Every program that sorts correctly for n items also works for n + 1 items. Does it then work for every n?
lesson.example:
Prove 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2. Base: n = 1 gives 1 = 1.
Step: if true for k, then 1 + … + k + (k + 1) = k(k + 1)/2 + (k + 1) = (k + 1)(k + 2)/2.

questions.q: What does modus tollens infer from p → q and ¬q?

topics.title: Relations, partial orders and lattices
topics.summary: Equivalence relations, partial orders, Hasse diagrams and lattices.
notes: An equivalence relation partitions a set into equivalence classes.
A partial order is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive; a Hasse diagram draws it without loops or implied edges.
A lattice is a poset where every pair has a least upper bound (join) and greatest lower bound (meet).
outcomes: Test whether a poset is a lattice

topics.title: Counting and recurrence relations
topics.summary: Permutations, combinations, inclusion–exclusion and solving recurrences.
notes: Inclusion–exclusion: |A ∪ B ∪ C| = Σ|A| − Σ|A ∩ B| + |A ∩ B ∩ C|.
Linear homogeneous recurrence aₙ = c₁aₙ₋₁ + c₂aₙ₋₂ is solved by roots of r² − c₁r − c₂ = 0.
Generating functions encode sequences as power series.

topics.title: Graphs, trees and algorithms
topics.summary: Connectivity, planar graphs, colouring and spanning trees.
notes: Euler's formula for connected planar graphs: V − E + F = 2.
Chromatic number χ(G) is the fewest colours so adjacent vertices differ; planar graphs need at most 4.
Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms find minimum spanning trees.

topics.title: Finite automata and regular languages
topics.summary: DFA, NFA, regular expressions and their equivalence.
notes: A DFA has exactly one transition per symbol from each state; an NFA may have several or ε-moves.
Every NFA can be converted to an equivalent DFA (subset construction).
Regular expressions, DFAs and NFAs describe the same class: regular languages.
outcomes: Design a DFA for a language
Convert an NFA to a DFA

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms, MCA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Asymptotic analysis and recurrences
topics.summary: Big-O, Ω, Θ, amortised analysis and the master theorem.
notes: Master theorem for T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n): compare f(n) with n^(log_b a).
Amortised analysis averages cost over a sequence of operations (e.g. dynamic array doubling is O(1) amortised per push).
Space complexity counts extra memory used.

topics.title: Stacks, queues, lists and hashing
topics.summary: Linear data structures and hash tables.
notes: Stacks (LIFO) and queues (FIFO) via arrays or linked lists; deques allow both ends.
Hashing maps keys to slots: h(k) = k mod m; collisions resolved by chaining or open addressing (linear and quadratic probing, double hashing).
Load factor α = n ÷ m; expected search time with chaining is O(1 + α).
outcomes: Implement a hash table with collision handling
Choose a linear structure for a task

topics.title: Balanced search trees and heaps
topics.summary: BSTs, AVL trees, B-trees and binary heaps.
notes: AVL trees keep balance factor in {−1, 0, 1} by rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL); height O(log n).
B-trees of order m keep nodes at least half full; used in databases and file systems.
A binary heap supports insert and extract-min in O(log n); heapsort is O(n log n).
outcomes: Insert into an AVL tree with rotations

lesson.hook: A BST built from sorted input becomes a linked list. How do AVL trees stop that?
lesson.example:
Insert 10, 20, 30 into an AVL tree: 10 becomes unbalanced (balance −2, RR case).
A left rotation at 10 makes 20 the root with children 10 and 30.

questions.q: What is the height bound of an AVL tree with n nodes?
questions.a: O(log n), about 1.44 log₂ n at most.

topics.title: Shortest paths and spanning trees
topics.summary: BFS, DFS, topological sort, Dijkstra, Bellman–Ford and Floyd–Warshall.
notes: Topological sort orders a DAG's vertices so every edge goes forward (DFS finishing times).
Dijkstra with a binary heap runs in O((V + E) log V); needs non-negative weights.
Bellman–Ford handles negative weights and detects negative cycles in O(VE).
outcomes: Run shortest path algorithms by hand

topics.title: Greedy, dynamic programming and backtracking
topics.summary: Design paradigms with classic examples.
notes: Greedy: Huffman coding, activity selection, fractional knapsack.
Dynamic programming: LCS, matrix chain multiplication, 0/1 knapsack, edit distance.
Backtracking: N-queens, subset sum, graph colouring; branch and bound for optimisation.
outcomes: Choose a design paradigm for a problem
Write a DP recurrence and fill its table

courses.title: Database Management Systems, MCA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: ER and relational models
topics.summary: ER modelling, mapping to relations and keys.
notes: ER constructs: entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality, participation, weak entities, specialisation and generalisation.
Mapping: each strong entity to a table; M:N relationships to a separate table with both keys.
Keys: super, candidate, primary, alternate, foreign.
outcomes: Model a domain as an ER diagram

topics.title: Relational algebra, calculus and advanced SQL
topics.summary: Query languages and advanced SQL features.
notes: Relational algebra operations: σ, π, ∪, −, ×, ⋈, ÷ (division for "for all" queries).
SQL features: joins, nested and correlated subqueries, views, window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, SUM OVER).
Triggers and stored procedures run logic inside the database.

lesson.example: Top earner per department: SELECT * FROM (SELECT e.*, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) r FROM emp e) t WHERE r = 1;

questions.q: Which relational algebra operator answers "students enrolled in all courses"?

topics.title: Dependencies and normal forms
topics.summary: Armstrong's axioms, closures, keys and normal forms up to BCNF and 4NF.
notes: Armstrong's axioms: reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity.
Attribute closure X⁺ finds all attributes determined by X; X is a superkey if X⁺ contains all attributes.
BCNF: every non-trivial FD X → Y has X a superkey; 4NF removes non-trivial multivalued dependencies.
outcomes: Compute attribute closures and candidate keys

topics.title: Indexing and query processing
topics.summary: File organisation, B+ tree and hash indexes, and query optimisation.
notes: B+ trees keep all records in leaves linked for range scans.
Clustered index orders the data file; a table has at most one.
Query optimisation chooses a plan by estimated cost; push selections down early.
outcomes: Choose an index for a workload

topics.title: Concurrency control and recovery
topics.summary: Serialisability, locking, timestamps and log-based recovery.
notes: Conflict serialisability is tested with a precedence graph (acyclic means serialisable).
Strict two-phase locking holds exclusive locks until commit, preventing cascading aborts.
Write-ahead logging: log records reach disk before data pages; ARIES uses analysis, redo and undo.

topics.title: NoSQL databases
topics.summary: Key-value, document, column-family and graph stores, and the CAP theorem.
notes: CAP theorem: a distributed system can guarantee only two of consistency, availability and partition tolerance at once.
BASE: basically available, soft state, eventually consistent.
Examples: Redis (key-value), MongoDB (document), Cassandra (column-family), Neo4j (graph).
outcomes: Choose a NoSQL model for an application

courses.title: Operating Systems, MCA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Process management and scheduling
topics.summary: Process concept, threads and CPU scheduling algorithms.
notes: Scheduling criteria: CPU utilisation, throughput, turnaround, waiting and response time.
Algorithms: FCFS, SJF/SRTF, priority, round robin, multilevel feedback queue.
User-level vs kernel-level threads; many-to-one, one-to-one and many-to-many models.

topics.title: Synchronisation and deadlocks
topics.summary: Critical sections, semaphores, monitors and deadlock handling.
notes: Peterson's solution satisfies mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting for two processes.
Monitors encapsulate shared data with condition variables (wait, signal).
Deadlock handling: prevention, avoidance (Banker's), detection with recovery, or ignoring (ostrich).

topics.title: Paging and virtual memory
topics.summary: Paging, TLBs, demand paging and replacement policies.
notes: Effective access time with TLB = h(t + m) + (1 − h)(t + 2m) for hit ratio h, TLB time t and memory time m.
Demand paging loads pages on a page fault.
LRU and optimal replacement do not suffer Belady's anomaly; FIFO can.

topics.title: File systems and disk management
topics.summary: File system structure, allocation, free-space management and RAID.
notes: Inodes store file metadata and block pointers (direct, single, double, triple indirect).
Free space: bitmap or linked list.
RAID 0 stripes, RAID 1 mirrors, RAID 5 stripes with distributed parity.
outcomes: Compute maximum file size with inodes

topics.title: Protection, security and virtual machines
topics.summary: Access control, threats and virtualisation.
notes: Access matrix implemented as access control lists or capability lists.
Threats: malware, buffer overflow, privilege escalation, denial of service.
Hypervisors (type 1 and 2) and containers isolate workloads.
outcomes: Design access control for a system
Explain virtualisation's role in the OS

courses.title: Object Oriented Programming with Java, MCA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: OOP in Java
topics.summary: Classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces.
notes: Java is platform-independent through bytecode and the JVM.
Interfaces may have default and static methods (Java 8+); a class implements many interfaces.
Abstract classes can hold state and constructors; interfaces cannot hold instance state.

topics.title: Collections framework and generics
topics.summary: List, Set, Map, iterators and generic types.
notes: ArrayList (fast random access), LinkedList (fast inserts), HashSet (unique, unordered), TreeSet (sorted), HashMap (key–value).
Generics give compile-time type safety: List<String>.
equals and hashCode must be overridden together for hash-based collections.
outcomes: Choose a collection for a problem

topics.title: Lambdas and streams
topics.summary: Lambda expressions, functional interfaces and the Stream API.
notes: A lambda implements a functional interface (one abstract method), e.g. Comparator, Predicate, Function.
Streams: source, intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted) and a terminal operation (collect, reduce, forEach).
Streams are lazy; intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation is called.

questions.q: What kind of interface can a lambda implement?
questions.a: A functional interface: one with a single abstract method.

topics.title: Multithreading and concurrency utilities
topics.summary: Threads, synchronisation and java.util.concurrent.
notes: ExecutorService manages thread pools; Future and CompletableFuture hold results.
synchronized, volatile and locks (ReentrantLock) control shared access.
Concurrent collections: ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue.

topics.title: JDBC and servlets
topics.summary: Connecting to databases and building server-side web components.
notes: JDBC steps: load driver, get Connection, create PreparedStatement, execute, process ResultSet, close.
PreparedStatement prevents SQL injection.
A servlet handles HTTP requests (doGet, doPost) in a container such as Tomcat; JSP mixes HTML with Java.

courses.title: Computer Networks, MCA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Layered models and performance
topics.summary: OSI and TCP/IP models, delay and throughput.
notes: Total delay = processing + queuing + transmission (L/R) + propagation (d/s).
Bandwidth–delay product = bandwidth × round-trip time.
Protocol layering gives modularity; encapsulation adds a header per layer.

topics.title: LANs and switching
topics.summary: Ethernet, MAC addressing, switches and VLANs.
notes: A MAC address is 48 bits; ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses.
Switches learn MAC addresses and forward frames; VLANs separate broadcast domains.
Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA with optional RTS/CTS.

topics.title: IP, subnetting and routing
topics.summary: IPv4, CIDR, NAT, IPv6 and routing protocols.
notes: CIDR a.b.c.d/n: 2^(32−n) addresses, 2^(32−n) − 2 usable hosts.
NAT maps private addresses (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) to public ones.
Intra-domain routing: RIP, OSPF; inter-domain: BGP.

questions.q: Split 192.168.10.0/24 into 4 equal subnets. What prefix?

topics.title: TCP reliability and congestion control
topics.summary: Sliding windows, flow control and congestion control.
notes: TCP connection: three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK); close with FIN.
Flow control uses the receiver's advertised window.
Congestion control: slow start (exponential), congestion avoidance (additive increase), multiplicative decrease on loss.

topics.title: Application protocols and network security
topics.summary: HTTP, DNS, email, and TLS and firewalls.
notes: HTTP/1.1 persistent connections; HTTP/2 multiplexes streams; HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (UDP).
DNS hierarchy: root, TLD, authoritative servers; records A, AAAA, MX, CNAME.
TLS provides confidentiality and integrity with certificates; firewalls filter packets by rules.
outcomes: Trace a web page request end to end

courses.title: Software Engineering, MCA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Plan-driven and agile processes
topics.summary: SDLC models, agile methods and DevOps.
notes: Agile Manifesto values individuals, working software, customer collaboration and responding to change.
Scrum roles: product owner, scrum master, developers; events: sprint, planning, daily scrum, review, retrospective.
DevOps combines development and operations with CI/CD pipelines.

topics.title: Requirements engineering
topics.summary: Elicitation, specification, validation and user stories.
notes: User story: "As a <role>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>", with acceptance criteria.
IEEE 830 / ISO 29148 describe SRS contents.
Requirements traceability links requirements to design, code and tests.
outcomes: Write user stories with acceptance criteria

topics.title: Architecture and design patterns
topics.summary: Architectural styles, UML and design patterns.
notes: Styles: layered, client–server, MVC, microservices, event-driven.
SOLID principles guide object-oriented design.
Patterns: creational (Singleton, Factory), structural (Adapter, Decorator), behavioural (Observer, Strategy).
outcomes: Choose an architecture for a system

topics.title: Testing strategies
topics.summary: Unit, integration, system and acceptance testing, and test design.
notes: Test-driven development writes a failing test first, then code, then refactors.
Black-box: equivalence classes, boundary values, decision tables; white-box: statement and branch coverage.
Regression testing re-runs tests after changes.

topics.title: Estimation, metrics and quality
topics.summary: Function points, COCOMO II, risk and quality models.
notes: Function points measure functionality from inputs, outputs, inquiries, files and interfaces.
Basic COCOMO effort E = a(KLOC)^b; development time D = c(E)^d.
Quality models: ISO 25010; process maturity: CMMI levels 1–5.
outcomes: Estimate effort with function points or COCOMO

courses.title: Web Technologies, MCA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: HTML5 and CSS3
topics.summary: Semantic HTML, forms, CSS layout and responsive design.
notes: Semantic elements (header, nav, main, article, footer) improve accessibility and SEO.
Box model: content, padding, border, margin; flexbox and grid lay out pages.
Media queries adapt layouts to screen sizes.
outcomes: Build a responsive page with flexbox or grid

topics.title: JavaScript and the DOM
topics.summary: Language basics, DOM manipulation, events and asynchronous code.
notes: let and const are block-scoped; === compares without type coercion.
The DOM is manipulated with querySelector, addEventListener and element properties.
Promises and async/await handle asynchronous operations such as fetch.
outcomes: Manipulate the DOM in response to events

topics.title: Node.js and Express
topics.summary: Server-side JavaScript and building REST APIs.
notes: Node.js runs JavaScript on an event loop with non-blocking I/O.
Express routes map HTTP methods and paths to handlers; middleware processes requests in order.
REST uses resources and HTTP verbs: GET read, POST create, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE remove.
outcomes: Build a REST API with Express

topics.title: JSON, databases and front-end frameworks
topics.summary: Data exchange and component-based front ends.
notes: JSON is the standard data format for web APIs.
Front-end frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) build UIs from components with state.
Single-page applications update the page without full reloads.
outcomes: Consume a JSON API in a front end

topics.title: Securing web applications
topics.summary: Common vulnerabilities and defences.
notes: OWASP Top 10 includes broken access control, injection, cryptographic failures and security misconfiguration.
Prevent XSS by escaping output; prevent SQL injection with parameterised queries; prevent CSRF with tokens.
Use HTTPS, secure cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) and hashed passwords (bcrypt, argon2).

courses.title: Python Programming for Data Science, MCA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Python for programmers
topics.summary: Data types, comprehensions, functions and modules.
notes: Lists, tuples, sets and dicts; comprehensions build them concisely.
Functions are first-class; decorators wrap functions.
Virtual environments (venv) isolate dependencies; pip installs packages.
outcomes: Manage packages in a virtual environment

topics.title: Data handling
topics.summary: Arrays, vectorisation, DataFrames, cleaning and grouping.
notes: NumPy broadcasting applies operations across arrays of compatible shapes.
pandas: loc (labels) and iloc (positions); dropna, fillna for missing data.
groupby-aggregate summarises data by category; merge joins DataFrames.

topics.title: Visualising data
topics.summary: Matplotlib and Seaborn plots for exploration.
notes: Choose charts by question: distribution (histogram, box plot), relationship (scatter), comparison (bar), trend (line).
Seaborn builds statistical plots on Matplotlib.
Label axes, units and titles; avoid misleading scales.
outcomes: Choose the right chart for a question

topics.title: Exploratory statistics
topics.summary: Descriptive statistics, correlation and sampling.
notes: describe() gives count, mean, std, min, quartiles and max.
Correlation (Pearson) measures linear association; it does not prove causation.
Train–test split avoids evaluating a model on the data it learned from.

topics.title: Building models
topics.summary: Regression, classification and evaluation with scikit-learn.
notes: Workflow: split, fit, predict, evaluate (fit on training data only).
Regression metrics: MAE, RMSE, R²; classification: accuracy, precision, recall, F1.
Pipelines combine preprocessing (scaling, encoding) and the model.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, MCA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Intelligent agents and search
topics.summary: Agent types, uninformed and informed search, and adversarial search.
notes: A* is optimal with an admissible heuristic (never overestimates) and complete in finite graphs.
Minimax with alpha–beta pruning searches game trees; best-case it examines about b^(d/2) nodes.
Constraint satisfaction uses backtracking with heuristics (MRV, forward checking).

topics.title: Regression and classification
topics.summary: Linear and logistic regression, decision trees, SVM and ensembles.
notes: Linear regression minimises squared error; regularisation (ridge L2, lasso L1) curbs overfitting.
Logistic regression models P(y = 1) = 1 ÷ (1 + e^(−z)).
Decision trees split on information gain (entropy) or Gini; random forests and gradient boosting combine many trees.
SVM finds the maximum-margin hyperplane; kernels handle non-linear data.
outcomes: Choose and train a supervised model

lesson.hook: A model scores 99% on training data and 60% on new data. What went wrong?
lesson.example:
Entropy of a node with 4 yes and 4 no = −(0.5 log₂ 0.5 + 0.5 log₂ 0.5) = 1 bit.
A split giving pure child nodes (entropy 0) has information gain 1 bit, the maximum.

questions.q: What does L1 regularisation tend to do to weights?
questions.a: Push some exactly to zero, giving sparse models.

topics.title: Clustering and dimensionality reduction
topics.summary: k-means, hierarchical clustering and PCA.
notes: k-means alternates assigning points to the nearest centroid and recomputing centroids; choose k by the elbow method or silhouette score.
Hierarchical clustering builds a dendrogram (agglomerative or divisive).
PCA projects data onto orthogonal directions of maximum variance (eigenvectors of the covariance matrix).

topics.title: Deep learning basics
topics.summary: Multilayer perceptrons, backpropagation, CNNs and RNNs.
notes: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute gradients; gradient descent updates weights: w ← w − η ∂L/∂w.
CNNs use convolution and pooling for images; RNNs and LSTMs process sequences.
Transformers use self-attention and underlie large language models.
outcomes: Explain how a network is trained

topics.title: Evaluation, validation and responsible AI
topics.summary: Cross-validation, metrics and fairness.
notes: k-fold cross-validation estimates generalisation error.
ROC curve plots TPR against FPR; AUC summarises it.
Responsible AI: fairness, transparency, privacy and accountability.
outcomes: Evaluate models with cross-validation and ROC
Identify bias risks in a model

courses.title: Cloud Computing, MCA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Service and deployment models
topics.summary: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, serverless and deployment models.
notes: Serverless (FaaS) runs functions on demand and bills per execution.
Deployment models: public, private, hybrid, multi-cloud.
Elasticity scales resources automatically with load.
outcomes: Choose a service model for a workload

topics.title: Virtual machines, Docker and Kubernetes
topics.summary: Hypervisors, containers and orchestration.
notes: Containers package an application with its dependencies; images are built from a Dockerfile.
Kubernetes orchestrates containers: pods, deployments, services, autoscaling.
Containers start faster and use fewer resources than VMs but share the host kernel.

topics.title: Designing for the cloud
topics.summary: Availability, scalability and cost.
notes: Availability zones and regions provide fault isolation; design for failure.
Load balancers spread traffic; auto-scaling groups add or remove instances.
Pay-as-you-go pricing; reserved and spot instances reduce cost.

topics.title: Cloud storage and databases
topics.summary: Object, block and file storage, and managed databases.
notes: Object storage (S3, Blob) for unstructured data; block storage for VM disks; file storage for shared file systems.
Managed relational (RDS, Cloud SQL) and NoSQL (DynamoDB, Firestore) databases.
Content delivery networks cache content near users.

topics.title: Cloud security
topics.summary: Identity and access management, encryption and compliance.
notes: Shared responsibility model divides security duties between provider and customer.
IAM follows least privilege; use roles rather than long-lived keys.
Encrypt data at rest and in transit; monitor with logging and audit trails.

courses.title: Big Data Analytics, MCA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Characteristics of big data
topics.summary: The Vs of big data and analytics types.
notes: Volume, velocity, variety, veracity and value.
Analytics types: descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive.
Data lakes store raw data; data warehouses store structured, modelled data.

topics.title: HDFS and MapReduce
topics.summary: Distributed storage and batch processing.
notes: HDFS splits files into blocks (128 MB default) replicated (3 by default) across DataNodes; the NameNode keeps metadata.
MapReduce: map emits key–value pairs, shuffle groups by key, reduce aggregates.
YARN manages cluster resources.

topics.title: Apache Spark
topics.summary: In-memory processing with RDDs and DataFrames.
notes: Spark keeps data in memory across stages, so iterative jobs run much faster than MapReduce.
Transformations (map, filter) are lazy; actions (count, collect) trigger execution.
Spark SQL, MLlib, Structured Streaming and GraphX extend the core.

topics.title: NoSQL stores and stream processing
topics.summary: Column-family and document stores, and Kafka.
notes: HBase and Cassandra store wide-column data for fast writes.
Kafka is a distributed log: producers write to topics; consumers read by offset.
Windowed aggregations process unbounded streams.
outcomes: Choose a store for a big data workload

topics.title: Analytics pipeline
topics.summary: ETL/ELT, data quality and dashboards.
notes: ETL transforms before loading; ELT loads then transforms in the warehouse.
Data quality dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness.
Dashboards present KPIs for decisions.

courses.title: Cyber Security (elective), MCA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MCA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: CIA triad and threats
topics.summary: Security goals, threats, vulnerabilities and attacks.
notes: CIA triad: confidentiality, integrity, availability.
Risk = Threat × Vulnerability × Impact (qualitatively).
Attacks: phishing, malware, ransomware, man-in-the-middle, DDoS, SQL injection.

topics.title: Symmetric, asymmetric and hashing
topics.summary: Encryption algorithms, digital signatures and PKI.
notes: Symmetric (AES) uses one shared key; asymmetric (RSA, ECC) uses public and private keys.
Hash functions (SHA-256) give fixed-size digests; they should be collision-resistant.
A digital signature signs a hash with the private key; certificates bind public keys to identities.
outcomes: Choose a cryptographic primitive for a need

topics.title: Firewalls, IDS and VPNs
topics.summary: Perimeter and network defences.
notes: Firewalls filter traffic (packet filter, stateful, application/next-generation).
IDS detects intrusions (signature or anomaly based); IPS also blocks them.
VPNs (IPsec, TLS) create encrypted tunnels.

topics.title: Secure development and cyber law in India
topics.summary: Secure coding, incident response and the legal framework.
notes: Secure SDLC: threat modelling, code review, testing (SAST, DAST), patching.
Incident response: preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned.
IT Act, 2000 offences (e.g. section 66 computer-related offences, 66C identity theft); CERT-In requires reporting incidents within 6 hours.
outcomes: Identify offences under the IT Act
